elena (sales): Heads-up — Kepler Health wants a POC. They plan to deploy a custom finetuned model kepler-med-13b-q4 (4-bit) via our hosted API with an option to move to Dedicated later. Requirements: KMS + audit logs, deterministic outputs for evals, p50 <200ms for ~8 tokens, sustained ~50 concurrent reqs. Security questionnaire incoming. Any immediate compatibility or pricing blockers? cc @mike @vivian

mike (solutions): Short answer: looks doable but a few gotchas. q4 path is supported by our runtime but this specific quant layout (grouped-quant + RMSNorm variant) may trigger fallback to slower kernels on hosted unless we enable the optimized kernel. Also deterministic outputs: we can seed RNG and pin configs but some ops (depending on the export) can be nondet across devices.

vivian (se): To add — KV cache will help latency for multi-turn, but for cold-starts and short generations caching impact is limited. For 8-token responses, kernel perf matters most. Can you confirm sample prompt length + max gen?

elena (sales): Typical prompt ~120 tokens, max gen 8. They run evals where exact string match matters across runs.

mike (solutions): OK — for deterministic evals we recommend: 1) freeze tokenization/version, 2) run evals in Private or Dedicated using customer KMS to avoid rollout differences, 3) pin model weights to a specific artifact sha. Even with those, we should run a determinism check suite. I can run a quick dry-run if they can share a small model shard or a docker artifact.

raj (infra): For their latency/throughput target (p50 <200ms @ 50 rps per model): hosted can do it but only with burst capacity and warm cache; cost will be much higher. Recommend Dedicated with 2 reserved GPUs of T4/A10-class or 1xA100 depending on batch/sequence distribution. I'll run an estimated perf calc if we get sample traces.

anya (security): Security notes: Hosted supports envelope encryption with our managed keys; customer-managed keys (CMK) with full audit/HSM export require Private deployment. Also need to answer their questionnaire about data residency + SOC2 logs — we can attach our SOC2 and KMS diagram. Please forward the questionnaire.

elena (sales): They asked for a ballpark committed price for Dedicated (monthly) vs hosted per-token for this workload. Any quick numbers?

mike (solutions): Ballpark: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) ~ $0.09–0.15 per 1k tokens for this heavy quantized model when accounting for kernel overhead + burst. Dedicated commit (monthly) — depends on GPU sizing; rough: $18k–30k/month for 2x A10-equivalent reserved with autoscale buffer. I'll confirm with pricing.

elena (sales): Perfect. I'll ask them for a short determinism test artifact and their security questionnaire. @anya can you prepare SOC2 + KMS diagram to attach?

anya (security): On it — will drop docs in the thread and flag items that require Private deployment.

mike (solutions): If they can share a small sample (1-2 prompts + model checksum) I can run a determinism + perf smoke test tomorrow. Example curl for hosted run:

    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n      -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n      -d '{"model":"kepler-med-13b-q4","input":"<sample prompt>","max_tokens":8}'

vivian (se): Also flag: if they plan to use KMS + audit logs we should scope whether logs contain PII; we can redact at ingest but need their approval.

elena (sales): Great — I'll collect artifacts and the questionnaire, then we can decide Hosted trial vs Dedicated POC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary build 2026-03-22T09:12:00 passed for quant-kernel-optimizer; this may resolve the hosted kernel fallback for grouped q4 variants.

mike (solutions): Nice — if that optimizer is available we can try hosted smoke first and fallback to Dedicated only if perf or determinism fails.

elena (sales): Closing loop with Kepler Health now, will post updates here.
